lessonsIntro: Woolacombe has two surf schools in the village, one right on the beach slipway, and a long sandy beach with room for lessons even in summer.

text: Woolacombe is a big, open beach that suits all levels. Beginners stay in the smaller waves close to shore, while more experienced surfers paddle further out, so there's usually space for lessons even when the beach is busy. Schools run sessions for complete beginners through to advanced surfers, and Woolacombe Surf Centre welcomes everyone from age 8, with tailored private sessions for younger children.

The RNLI describes Woolacombe as a family beach with good surf, and in peak season there are two patrolled bathing areas when conditions allow. Lifeguards are on duty daily from early May to late September, plus Easter, some October weekends and October half term. Outside those dates there may be no cover at all, so if there are no flags, there are no lifeguards. Book a lesson rather than heading out alone on your first day.

hireIntro: Woolacombe has plenty of hire, from the slipway on the beach to shops a short walk up in the village.

text: Start on a fully soft board such as a SoftDog, then move to a semi-soft Softech or a mid-length as you improve. Surf guides describe Woolacombe's summer waves as fat and friendly, with much tougher conditions in winter. The sea here runs from about 15-18C in mid-August to 8-9C in early March. Wear a 3/2mm or 4/3mm in summer, and a 5/4mm or thicker with boots, gloves and a hood in early spring.

shopsIntro: Woolacombe has several surf shops within walking distance of the beach, selling boards, wetsuits and accessories.
shopsText: Surfing Woolacombe's shop sits on the slipway, steps from the sand, and doubles as a Softech test centre. Up in the village, The Bay Surf Shop on Barton Road stocks boards, wetsuits and bodyboards all year, and Shore 2 Surf on West Road is a family-run shop with boards, wetsuits and accessories. Saltrock also has a Woolacombe store for surf clothing.

lessons.a: Yes. Beginners learn in the smaller waves near the shore, and both village schools teach complete beginners.
Woolacombe Surf Centre welcomes surfers from age 8, and offers tailored private sessions for under-8s if you contact them.
In 2026 the RNLI patrols daily from 2 May to 27 September, 10am to 6pm, plus Easter, some October weekends and October half term.

hire.q: Can I hire a board right on the beach?
hire.a: Yes. Surfing Woolacombe hires boards, bodyboards, SUPs and wetsuits from its base on the beach slipway.

hire.q: Can I hire for a whole week?
hire.a: Surfing Woolacombe offers hourly, daily and weekly hire.

shops.q: Can I try a board before buying?
shops.a: Surfing Woolacombe is a Softech test centre, so you can rent a board before you buy one.

shops.q: Are the shops open in winter?
shops.a: The Bay Surf Shop says it stocks kit all year round.
